shells of cars moving everywhere, bumpers being attached,

the vast majority of brand new cars sold around the world today
are still guzzling petrol. And given most new cars
run for at least 20 years. That's a lot of tailpipes spewing a lot of greenhouse gases for a very

I of course answer this question in the AMA, which you can listen to on the previous episode,
but here I'll answer more in depth.
This is the thought process I guide myself through when I'm in the land of too many ideas must pick one.
There are three assumptions embedded in too many ideas, must pick one.
1. All these ideas are equally likely to succeed.
2. I'm equally capable of succeeding at each of these ideas.
3. I can't work on multiple ideas at once.
Let's look at each of those. If you feel you have too many ideas,
you must think they're equally likely to succeed, which is the first assumption.

You may feel each idea is equally likely to succeed because each idea is likely to get

If you have a clearer picture of what forms of success are more important to you than

Question 2.
